events.title: Lebombo closure during Mozambique election unrest
events.direction: Both directions affected, with selective homeward returns to each country; exact chronology differs by side and category.
events.movement: Travellers and freight, with intermittent homeward movements and selective truck releases
events.exceptions: Homebound Mozambican nationals admitted during November6/7 temporary opening; perishable/fuel trucks reportedly released; later homebound people, empty return trucks and recovery vehicles. Timing and exact category bounds remain incomplete.
events.enforcement: Primary BMA closure notice and dated South African reporting establish closure and temporary passage; Mozambican reporting supplies separately attributed side-specific reopening accounts.
events.relationship: One interrupted regime retained under stable SC05; no new duplicate phase rows. Earlier temporary openings, November7 reclosure and November8/9 restoration milestones recorded explicitly; later recurrence SC26 remains separate.
events.status_observation: Historical evidence only; current status not inferred
events.official_rationale: Public safety after vehicles were burned on the Mozambican side
events.context: Post-election unrest produced repeated interruption and partial passage at Lebombo/Ressano Garcia. The November5 closure was interrupted before the previously recorded November8 partial opening; cargo/full-restoration accounts follow November9.
events.uncertainty: SABC quotes a Wednesday November6 partial reopening lasting overnight; EWN describes Thursday November7 morning opening before renewed closure. Rádio Moçambique on November8 attributes homeward opening on its side to November7 afternoon. These may describe different side/category phases; timing is unresolved. November8 is not the first relaxation. No continuous November5–8 closure retained. Later recurrence remains SC26.

historical.duration_note: No exact continuous interval. Temporary homebound passage before November8 and renewed closure invalidate the former November5–8 three-day spell. November8 retained solely as a later partial-opening milestone.

events.scope: National road and rail passenger travel
events.crossings: Kazungula road/ferry; Ngoma; Ramokgwebana; Martins Drift; Ramatlabama; Tlokweng; Mamuno; Pioneer; Mohembo reopened
events.direction: Entry into and exit from Botswana, subject to returnee/essential-movement exceptions; calculated interval scoped to ordinary passengers at Tlokweng.
events.movement: Non-exempt ordinary passengers; freight and defined essential movement excepted.
events.exceptions: Returning citizens subject to quarantine; closely monitored essential services and commodities, including links with South Africa and Zambia.
events.enforcement: BOPA March26 Tlokweng report records March24 measures in effect, quoted port-health refusals and returnees taken to quarantine. December2 report records actual December1 passenger traffic. Neither is a survey of every post or intervening day.

events.official_rationale: COVID-19 containment
events.context: Closure documented by WHO on 2 April; ten commercial land crossings reopened for passengers in December.
events.uncertainty: 252-day interval is the scoped ordinary-passenger policy phase at Tlokweng, not all-traffic closure. Newly inspected November9 legal notice schedules December1 ground reopening; actual Tlokweng traffic is documented separately. Other posts remain policy/reporting evidence, without independent gate-by-gate verification. Current WHO-page retrieval timed out; prior evidence preserved.

historical.duration_note: Calendar-date difference to the stated partial reopening for the specified category and crossing; not exact hours or universal closure. 252 days describes the non-exempt ordinary-passenger phase at Tlokweng, from March 24 to observed December 1 passage. Preserve correlated alternatives and withhold the spurious independent 0–2-day arithmetic; no actual reopening is inferred. Electoral administration and public-order security are explicitly reported ministerial purposes. The order is not evidence of a distinct trade or migration rationale. The government page and Anadolu were directly read; Anadolu repeats the government origin. L-Frii was available only as indexed text after direct 429. The precise signed order remains missing. The phase remains unlocated and limited to an announced-window display rule. No national physical-enforcement geometry is inferred.
